relevant_findings.finding: Door frame set consists of three jamb pieces (left, right, head) and door stop molding. Stop is the small ledge the door closes against, typically 7/16" x 1-3/8" material applied to the frame.
Frames are estimated per-opening (EA), not per linear foot like trim. Production workflow is per-opening: access opening, prep frame, coat frame, move to next.

Per PCA standards, any surface less than 1 foot in width or height is measured as 1 LF per LF (or 1 SF per SF). A 4-inch wide frame and a 6-inch wide frame are both counted as 1 LF — no distinction. Frame width does NOT affect measurement or production rate.

Taller doors (7'0", 8'0") have more linear footage of frame material, therefore more paintable surface. This is captured in the LF/EA quantity naturally — no separate modifier needed. Height access modifiers (ladder work) are separate from surface area.

Factory primer is transit protection, not finish-ready primer. Always assess condition. Intact/clean = scuff sand 180-grit, may proceed with or without field primer. Damaged/scratched = spot prime. Weathered/chalking = full sand, full prime.

Interior door frames use same coating systems as door slabs. QT3 = standard acrylic enamel (SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC). QT4 = modified urethane (SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE). QT5 = premium urethane or Gallery Series (SYS_FF_PREMIUM).
Interstage (inspect-repair-sand cycle) runs after each coat EXCEPT final coat. Same process at all quality tiers — only scrutiny level varies.

When doors are installed before painting complete, hinge mortises and strike mortises need touch-up. Installer routing/chiseling exposes bare wood. Touch-up is per-hinge (typically 3) and per-strike (1).
Pocket door frames have no door stop (door slides into wall). Reduced paintable surface. Split jamb design may affect access to header portion.
Cased openings (no door) have frame jambs but no stop and no hardware mortises. Simplified scope compared to standard door frames.
Bifold door frames have jambs and head but use track hardware instead of hinges. Stop configuration differs from standard swing doors. Include in frame_type as distinct variant.

Door frames can be finished via brush/roll using Roll and Tip methodology. Work jamb surfaces with small roller (4"), tip with 2-2.5" angled sash brush. Inside corners require careful technique to avoid buildup. For waterborne products: apply, tip once, walk away.

Open time varies significantly by coating chemistry. Oil-based has longest working time. Standard waterborne enamel has moderate open time. Modified urethane / waterborne urethane (like Advance) has SHORT open time (5-10 minutes) — do not overwork these products.

condition_drivers.impact: Controls whether primer coat is required. Factory primed may skip field primer at QT3; bare wood always requires primer.
Controls task inclusion. Pocket = no stop tasks. Cased_opening = no stop tasks, no mortise touch-up. Bifold = track hardware instead of hinge mortises.
Controls protection zone selection and production rates. Spray requires wall_adjacent_door and floor_full_8ft_radius zones. Brush/roll uses floor_workzone only.

quality_differences.description: Quick glance inspection at 6 feet. Fill obvious defects. Light scuff sand between coats. Standard acrylic enamel acceptable.
quality_differences.defect_tolerance: Minor brush marks, light orange peel acceptable

quality_differences.description: Systematic scan at 3 feet. Fill all visible defects. Full sand between coats 220 grit. Modified urethane for superior leveling.
Lighted critical inspection at arm's length. Fill every defect regardless of size. Thorough sand 220-320 grit. Premium urethane enamel.

failure_modes.cause: Factory primer degraded from weather exposure during construction or contaminated with construction dust/grease.
failure_modes.prevention: Assess factory primer condition. Scuff sand minimum. Apply bonding primer if adhesion test fails.

failure_modes.mode: Runs and sags on jamb surfaces
failure_modes.cause: Over-application on vertical surfaces. Jamb sides are prone to runs due to vertical orientation and confined space.
failure_modes.prevention: Light coats. Proper spray technique or brush load. For brush/roll: apply thin, tip once, walk away (§ 15.7.2).

failure_modes.cause: Stop applied with nails creates small dents/holes at junction. Paint bridges but telegraphs through.
failure_modes.prevention: Fill nail holes at stop-jamb junction during prep. Sand smooth before prime.

failure_modes.cause: Touch-up applied after main coats have cured. Different application method (brush vs spray) creates sheen/texture difference.
failure_modes.prevention: Schedule mortise touch-up during final coat application. Use same product and method.

failure_modes.cause: Excess material deposited in frame corners during brush application.
failure_modes.prevention: Load brush lightly, work coating out of corner onto flat surfaces. Do not deposit excess in corner (§ 15.11.1).

failure_modes.cause: Overworking modified urethane/waterborne urethane products that have short open time (5-10 minutes).
failure_modes.prevention: Apply, tip once, walk away. Do not go back. If defects remain, sand and recoat — do not try to fix while wet.

notes_for_materials_manager: Material system follows Fine Finish Doctrine: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC for QT3, SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE for QT4, SYS_FF_PREMIUM for QT5.
Primer system: acrylic primer for new/factory-primed; bonding primer if adhesion questionable; shellac spot prime for knots on bare wood frames.

OPEN TIME NOTE: Modified urethane / waterborne urethane (Advance, Emerald Urethane) have SHORT open time (5-10 min). Standard waterborne enamel has moderate open time. Oil-based has longest working time. Select product based on application skill and conditions.
Consumables: 2-2.5" angled sash brush for cutting in stop and jamb corners; 4" mini roller optional for jamb flats.
Caulk: painter's caulk for frame-to-drywall gap at reveal. Included in prep materials.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Module structure should mirror Fine Finish workflow: SETUP → INITIAL_PREP → [PRIME] → INTERSTAGE → FINISH_COAT_1 → INTERSTAGE → FINISH_COAT_2 → FINAL_INSPECT → CLEANUP.
Stop is painted as part of frame coat task — not a separate module. Stop surfaces are coated in same pass as jamb.
Mortise touch-up tasks are CONDITIONAL on installation_sequence configuration. If doors installed before painting, include mortise touch-up.
frame_type drives task inclusion: pocket excludes stop tasks; cased_opening excludes stop AND mortise tasks; bifold has track hardware instead of hinge mortises.
Protection setup should declare floor_workzone for brush/roll, upgrade to floor_full_8ft_radius + wall_adjacent_door for spray.
For brush/roll method: reference Roll and Tip technique (§ 15.6). Apply, tip once, walk away for modified urethane products.
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Primary UOM is EA (frame set). One frame set = one door opening.
Base production rate is FASTER than door slab — frame has less detail, no panel complexity, simpler geometry.
NO frame width modifier. Per PCA standards, surfaces <1 ft width are measured as 1 LF. A 4" frame and 6" frame are equivalent.
Taller doors (7'0", 8'0") have more LF of frame naturally — no separate height-surface modifier needed.

Height ACCESS modifier applies if door opening is in high-ceiling space (transom windows, tall doors). Use H2 for 9-12 ft head height, H3 for 13+ ft. This is for ladder/scaffold access, not surface area.
Quality tier modifiers follow standard registry: QT3=1.0, QT4=1.30, QT5=1.50.
Mortise touch-up is per-EA (per door), not per-hinge. Lump as single touch-up task per frame set.
Application method affects rate: brush/roll typically 1.15-1.25x spray time for equivalent quality.

assumptions.note: Doors Doctrine lists per-hinge times but practical estimation bundles as single touch-up task per frame.

uncertainties.description: Split jamb design on pocket frames may limit access to head jamb. Need to verify if header is typically painted as part of frame or handled separately.
uncertainties.recommended_action: Field validation on next pocket door project

uncertainties.description: Bifold frames may have different stop configurations than standard swing doors. Need to verify typical stop arrangement.
uncertainties.recommended_action: Field validation on next bifold door project

zones.notes: Drop cloth under door opening for drips during brush/roll work
Mask wall area adjacent to frame opening during spray
Mask hinges if doors are hung. Not needed if frames painted before door installation.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Frame and casing typically same color. Casing applied over frame reveal — painted together or sequentially with no cut-in needed.
Door edge meets frame stop when closed. Usually same color. If different, door edge is cut-in during slab painting, not frame painting.
Frame meets drywall at reveal edge. Typically caulked and painted as part of frame prep. No cut-in at runtime — caulk seals the junction.
Stop is part of frame set — always same finish. Bundled in same coating task.

affected_conditions.notes: Floor protection only when finished floors present. NC often has subfloor during frame painting.
Additional protection for occupied spaces. Rare in NC but possible for phased projects.
Lead protocols. Not applicable for true NC but may apply to NC-context remodels.
Tall door openings (8'0" doors, transoms above) may require ladder access for head jamb.

required_paintscope_keys.purpose: Count of door frame sets (one per opening)
Validation: frame count should match door opening count
Floor protection area under work zone
Wall masking adjacent to door opening for spray

research_corrections.original_claim: Frame width modifier of 1.20x for wide frames (6-9/16"+)
research_corrections.corrected_to: No frame width modifier. Per PCA standards, surfaces <1 ft width are measured as 1 LF regardless of actual width.

research_corrections.original_claim: Waterborne alkyd preferred for brush/roll due to longer open time
research_corrections.corrected_to: Modified urethane / waterborne urethane (Advance, Emerald Urethane) have SHORT open time (5-10 min). Standard waterborne enamel has moderate open time. Oil-based has longest working time.

qt2_scope_analysis.summary: QT2 for NC door frame finish is economy-grade trim work with minimal prep, reduced inspection intensity, and relaxed defect tolerance. Same sheen (semi-gloss standard for trim) but faster execution through reduced interstage rigor. Application quality (no drips/sags/runs) remains constant at all tiers.

included_tasks.qt2_behavior: Light scuff sand only (180 grit). Skip detailed defect fill. Address only obvious holes/damage.
included_tasks.notes: Factory primed frames: scuff sand and proceed. Bare wood: primer required but minimal fill.

included_tasks.qt2_behavior: Standard protection setup per application method. Binary task — same at all tiers.
included_tasks.notes: Floor workzone for brush/roll, floor_full_8ft_radius + wall_adjacent_door for spray.

included_tasks.qt2_behavior: Primer as needed based on substrate_condition. Binary task — application quality constant.
included_tasks.notes: Factory primed intact may skip field primer at QT2. Bare wood requires primer.

included_tasks.qt2_behavior: Two finish coats standard (trim convention). Application quality NOT reduced at QT2.
included_tasks.notes: Drips, sags, runs, holidays fail at ALL tiers including QT2. QT2 time savings come from reduced interstage work.

included_tasks.qt2_behavior: Quick visual at 8-10 ft, ambient lighting, single pass. Address only obvious failures.
included_tasks.notes: QT2 tolerance: minor brush marks, light orange peel acceptable. Heavy runs/drips still fail.

included_tasks.qt2_behavior: Standard cleanup. Binary task — same at all tiers.

excluded_tasks.reason: QT2 skips detailed spackle/fill. Only obvious holes addressed. Minor imperfections acceptable.

reduced_tasks.qt3_behavior: Inspect at 6 ft, mark visible defects, sand marked areas
reduced_tasks.qt2_behavior: Quick glance, sand entire surface lightly (no marking/targeted repair)

reduced_tasks.qt3_behavior: Full sand 180-220 grit, focus on defect areas
reduced_tasks.qt2_behavior: Light scuff sand 180 grit, no targeted repair

reduced_tasks.qt3_behavior: Fill defects found during interstage inspection
reduced_tasks.qt2_behavior: Skip interstage defect repair. Only address if defect will cause coating failure.
reduced_tasks.rate_adjustment: QT2 saves ~5-10 min per frame set on interstage repair

inspection_standard.comparison_to_qt3: QT3 is 6 ft with marking of visible defects

acceptable_at_qt2: Minor brush marks (visible but not heavy)
Minor sanding scratches if covered by finish

disclaimers: QT2 is economy-grade trim — suitable for rental properties, investment units, builder-grade spec homes
Sheen is NOT reduced at QT2 — semi-gloss is standard for trim at all tiers
Two finish coats remain standard at QT2 — single coat on trim is not acceptable
Application quality (drips/sags/runs) is NOT tiered — these fail at all quality levels
QT2 time savings come from reduced prep intensity and interstage rigor, not from faster or sloppier application

sheen_options.notes: Semi-gloss is standard for door frames at all tiers. High-gloss (QT4+) requires premium urethane system.

qt2_scope_analysis.nc_specific_notes: NC door frames are typically factory primed. QT2 may proceed directly over factory primer with light scuff sand (no field primer) if factory primer is intact and clean. This is a significant time savings vs QT3+ which may require more rigorous primer condition assessment.
